the phyllothers of 100 degC and 130 degC are not suitable for predicting leaf emergence of winter wheat and barley, respectively.

the phyllothem value should be set at 100 degCd for the prediction of the three upper leaves in winter wheat and barley.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a phyllothermic value of 100 degC is more appropriate than 130 degCd for predicting leaf emergence in the three last leaves to emergence in winter cereals.

the current phyllothermic value for predicting leaf appearance in wheat and barley (i.e. 130 degCd) is too high, resulting in a delay of fungicide applications and thus, a reduced efficacy against foliar disease pathogens.
